A reviewer agent finds three problems on a page and writes them in the chat. The implementing agent fixes the first one. Then the chat gets compacted, or the session restarts, and the other two findings drop out of its context.

The messages might still be there somewhere. But now the work depends on the agent finding them again, or on someone remembering they existed.

In this video, our CTO Vlad Luzin explains why pasting every chat into every agent doesn't fix it. That gives every agent more to read and makes the few things that matter harder to find. What has to survive is much smaller: the two open findings, who owns them, and whether they've been resolved.

BAND Desktop keeps that as shared work outside any one agent's session. Each agent gets the context it needs, and its working context doesn't turn into the team's filing cabinet.

The chat can be temporary. The work the team is relying on can't be.

See you at Reversim on December 1!

A group of us from BAND will be at TLV Expo for the day, and we want to talk to anyone running more than one coding agent. How do you split the work between them, how do they hand things off, and where do you still end up passing notes between them yourself?

That last part is what BAND for Developers is built to take off your plate. Your coding agents communicate, delegate and hand off work directly, and BAND Desktop shows you who owns what, what's stuck and what's waiting on you.

Find us there and say hi.

Google Antigravity agents can now join your team in BAND.

If you have the Antigravity CLI, go to Settings → Integrations in BAND Desktop and turn it on. BAND installs Google's Antigravity ACP server for you, and Antigravity shows up as a runtime when you create a new agent. Sign in with Google, pick the model and session mode, and you're set.

From there it works with the rest of your coding agents, handing work back and forth with them. It asks you questions in the room and shows its plans in BAND Desktop.

Building your own agents? Python SDK 7.1 adds an Antigravity ACP adapter, with a runnable example in the docs.

https://lnkd.in/ecciZv2V

Restart an agent and three weeks of decisions disappear with it. cognee's new integration gives any BAND agent a memory that outlasts the room. Each BAND room becomes a Cognee session: before your agent answers, it recalls what's relevant, and after it answers, the exchange is stored and later consolidated into a knowledge graph. It wraps the adapter you already have, so LangGraph, Anthropic, CrewAI, and Pydantic AI agents get it without touching their prompts.

The memory is also shared. Tell Claude Code something in your terminal, let it sync, then ask your BAND agent in a room. It knows.

We wrote it up with the Cognee team, including why a memory outage should never come out as "I have no record of that." Read now: https://lnkd.in/eb5crKyk

You come back from lunch to three agent chats, each one now thousands of pages long, and one simple question: where are we?

The answer is in there somewhere. To find it, you cross-reference the original plan with tool output, corrections, review comments, and newer messages that replaced earlier decisions. Then you do it twice more.

Chat is good at showing why an agent made a decision and how it reached a result. It's much worse at telling you what's true right now: what's done, what's left, what's blocked, and whether anyone needs your input.

In this video, our CTO Vlad Luzin shows how BAND desktop separates those two jobs. The reasoning stays in the chat for when you need it. The current state of the work stays on screen, so you don't reread the history to find it.

Every group of agents you add brings its own wall of text, and every wall keeps growing. The current state should stay simple enough to read at a glance.
